facts.text: The only major-college player of the 1960s to make 300 free throws: Pete Maravich, 1969-70 — 337-436 FT.
Only two major-college players of the 1960s attempted 800 field goals: Pete Maravich (3×, best 1969-70: 522-1168 FG); Elvin Hayes (1967-68: 519-945 FG).
The only major-college team of the 1960s to go unbeaten (20+ games) was UCLA — and it did it twice (1966-67: 30-0; 1963-64: 30-0).
Just three major-college players of the 1960s attempted 350 free throws: Pete Maravich (2×, best 1969-70: 337-436 FT); Len Chappell (1961-62: 278-383 FT); Terry Dischinger (1961-62: 292-350 FT).
Only two major-college teams of the 1960s won 30 games: Houston (1967-68: 31-2); UCLA (2×, best 1966-67: 30-0).
Just three major-college players of the 1960s averaged 22 rebounds a game (15+ games): Paul Silas (1961-62: 22.5 rpg); Artis Gilmore (1969-70: 22.2 rpg); Spencer Haywood (1968-69: 22.1 rpg).
Most 90-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) in the 1960s: Loyola (IL), 4 (1961-62, 1962-63, 1963-64, 1965-66).
13 major-college players grabbed 500 rebounds in the 1960s (18 seasons). The most extreme: Paul Silas, 1963-64 — 631 rebounds.
Most 25-point-per-game seasons (15+ games) by one school's players in the 1960s: Purdue, 7 (Rick Mount, Dave Schellhase, Terry Dischinger).
Highest rebounding average in a season in the 1960s: Paul Silas, Creighton, 1961-62 — 22.5 rpg.
Most 200-free-throw seasons by one school's players in the 1960s: Purdue, 5 (Terry Dischinger, Dave Schellhase, Rick Mount).
Best field-goal percentage in a season (200+ attempts) in the 1960s: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, UCLA, 1966-67 — 0.667%.
Best free-throw percentage in a season (100+ attempts) in the 1960s: Tommy Boyer, Arkansas, 1961-62 — 0.933%.
Highest team scoring average in a season in the 1960s: Syracuse, 1965-66 — 99.0 ppg (22-6).
Most wins in a season in the 1960s: Houston, 1967-68 — 31-2.
10 major-college players scored 900 points in the 1960s (12 seasons). The most extreme: Pete Maravich, 1969-70 — 1,381 pts in 31 games.
Highest scoring average in a season in the 1960s: Pete Maravich, Louisiana State, 1969-70 — 44.5 ppg.
Most points in a season in the 1960s: Pete Maravich, Louisiana State, 1969-70 — 1,381.
Most free throws made in a season in the 1960s: Pete Maravich, Louisiana State, 1969-70 — 337.
12 major-college teams averaged 95 points a game (15+ games) in the 1960s (15 seasons). The most extreme: Syracuse, 1965-66 — 99.0 ppg, 22-6.
Most rebounds of the 1960s: Paul Silas, 1,751.
Most points of the 1960s: Pete Maravich, 3,667.
Most free throws made in the 1960s: Pete Maravich, 893.
8 major-college players averaged 35 points a game (15+ games) in the 1960s (10 seasons). The most extreme: Pete Maravich, 1969-70 — 44.5 ppg.
28 major-college players averaged 30 points a game (15+ games) in the 1960s (35 seasons). The most extreme: Pete Maravich, 1969-70 — 44.5 ppg.
19 major-college players averaged 25 points and 15 rebounds (15+ games) in the 1960s (25 seasons). The most extreme: Billy McGill, 1961-62 — 38.8 ppg, 15.0 rpg.
5 major-college teams lost just once (20+ games) in the 1960s (6 seasons). The most extreme: UCLA, 1968-69 — 29-1.
19 major-college teams lost 22 games in the 1960s (23 seasons). The most extreme: Denver, 1968-69 — 2-24.
13 major-college players averaged 20 rebounds a game (15+ games) in the 1960s (16 seasons). The most extreme: Paul Silas, 1961-62 — 22.5 rpg.

method: College basketball (men's): each line is one Stathead (Sports Reference college basketball) Season Finder query over the decade's ten seasons (a decade is the seasons starting in its years: the 1970s run 1970-71 to 1979-80), run in a signed-in subscriber session; result rows and stable ids are stored as provenance.

Sports Reference's season finders begin with 1947-48, so the 1940s page covers two seasons and earlier decades are not in the record. Rebounds, assists, steals, blocks and the three-pointer (1986-87) arrive at different times; rules on a stat a season lacks return nothing. Per-game figures are totals divided by games.
